title: Supplier due diligence review
text: SYNTHETIC TRAINING CASE. HarborPay Demo, its service, documents, roles, facts and control states are fictional. This is an analyst-work-product example, not an audit, vendor attestation, legal opinion, or actual supplier decision. Assessment date: 16 November 2026 . Prepared for a fictional payroll service owner; human approval is pending. Decision in brief Recommendation: hold production onboarding pending evidence and authorized review. The service is modelled as high criticality because it processes employee identity, payroll and bank-account data and supports payroll operations. That is a proposed lab tier, not a validated business classification. The present packet does not establish current, authentic assurance over the purchased payroll service, and the initial customer MFA fixture is disabled. No evidence here establishes a breach or a vendor control failure. Request a current in-scope independent report and verifiable certificate, or a security-reviewer-validated alternative evidence package proportionate to this service; an ISO certificate alone would not answer operational-control, contract, subprocessor or continuity questions. A conditional path may be considered only by an authorized business risk owner after contractual protections, minimum controls, compensating safeguards, dated actions and stop/escalation triggers are evaluated. Any exception requires that accountable human approval; it is not an automatic bypass. Option When it could be justified Assessment here --- --- --- Onboard Current in-scope independent assurance or a security-reviewer-validated alternative evidence package; material contract and control requirements resolved; authorized owner accepts residual risk Not supported by this synthetic packet Conditional onboarding Documented risk authority, restricted use/data, effective compensating safeguards, dated conditions and stop/escalation triggers; exception approved by accountable human risk owner Possible only after evidence review and approval; conditions are not yet demonstrated Hold Material uncertainties affect sensitive data/service and minimum decision evidence or customer controls are unresolved Recommended pending current assurance, MFA verification and contract/operational diligence Scope and method The case concerns a payroll-processing SaaS handling employee identity, payroll and bank-account details. The review considers the actual service boundary, evidence currency/authenticity, shared responsibility, and treatment ownership. Framework references are question prompts mapped to selected NIST CSF 2.0 outcomes and ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Annex A themes in [ case-study/control_catalog.json ](../case-study/control_catalog.json); they are not a full controls audit or compliance conclusion. Read the original synthetic exhibits in [ case-study/evidence-packet/ ](../case-study/evidence-packet/). Evidence interpretation - E01 — certificate claim: It states a validity period ending 31 October 2026, before this assessment, and lacks issuer, accreditation details, certificate number, authoritative verification, and underlying certificate. Its declared payroll wording is not authenticated. Record CERT-EXPIRY as stale/unverified assurance. Expiry does not prove a control failed, a breach happened, or the supplier is unsafe. Ask for current verifiable evidence and validate legal entity, exact scope/sites/exclusions, certification body, accreditation chain, validity/status and any suspension. - E02 v1 — Type II-style summary: Its stated 1 January–30 September 2026 period is historical. The only stated system is a customer support portal; payroll is explicitly excluded. Therefore it is out of scope for this review, irrespective of its recent-looking dates. The report itself, criteria, opinion, tests, exceptions and subservice/CUEC schedules are absent. “Not represented” means unknown, not no exceptions. - E02-v2 — simulated scope edit: The revised fixture lists payroll and removes the exclusion. It changes a declared field only. It cannot authenticate the report, prove payroll was in the original examined boundary, supply period testing, exceptions/opinion, or establish actual control operation. Keep ASSURANCE-SCOPE open for a real review even if a software fixture check changes state. - SOC 2 Type II considerations: A genuine Type II report describes a system and reports on controls over a period. Review the actual service-organization description, opinion, criteria, tests/results, exceptions and management responses. Establish whether named subservice organizations are included or carved out; for a carve-out, identify dependencies and review the service auditor reports and complementary subservice-organization controls as appropriate. Review customer CUECs as conditions for the service organization's controls to achieve their objectives. The exercise E03 MFA CUEC is separately assigned to the fictional customer; do not imply it appeared in a real report. - Bridge statement: The synthetic E02-B prompt describes management's hypothetical no-material-change claim from 1 October to 16 November. No signed letter or corroboration exists. Even if received, such a letter would not extend the assurance period, test controls in the gap, show absence of incidents, or replace the independent report. Verify authority, coverage, incidents, changes and downstream-provider changes; leave the gap explicit. - E03 — customer CUEC: The customer is responsible for MFA on privileged payroll-admin accounts; v1's mock state is disabled. This is a customer-side prerequisite, not a HarborPay finding. E03-v2 marks MFA enabled in a labelled mock only. A real check needs the full privileged identity population, enforcement settings, exceptions/break-glass treatment and dated evidence. Keep real-world implementation unverified. - E04 — access-policy fixture: It asserts policy presence, approval date (1 October) and payroll scope. It supplies no full controlled policy or samples. It cannot evidence that access reviews, least privilege, MFA or deprovisioning operated effectively. Question-by-question review “Not established” is intentionally distinct from “failed.” IDs refer to the ten original questions in case-study/control_catalog.json . Each follow-up is a proposed request, not an assertion about HarborPay. Control question Evidence and reasoned result Gap / next request Proposed owner and target --- --- --- --- TPRM-GOV-01 Criticality and pre-engagement diligence data.json describes payroll and sensitive identity/bank data; it proposes High criticality and names fictional role owners. This supports a scenario rationale, not an approved organization tier or completed real pre-contract assessment. Business owner to confirm volumes, data flows, access, business impact, alternatives/concentration, jurisdictions and tier. Payroll service owner + security reviewer; before decision TPRM-GOV-02 Risk ownership and lifecycle data.json provides role labels and assessment date; no approved lifecycle procedure, named approver, review cadence or completed history. Confirm accountable risk-acceptance authority, procurement/security roles, annual and event-triggered reassessment, escalation and exit owners. Business relationship owner; before decision TPRM-CON-01 Contractual security obligations No executed agreement, security schedule or shared-responsibility contract exhibit is in the packet. Review incident notification deadlines/cooperation, audit/evidence rights, encryption/access duties, data location/return/deletion, subprocessor notice/objection, continuity, material change and termination clauses. Confirm privacy/DPA terms with legal/privacy. Procurement/legal + privacy/security; before production data TPRM-SUP-01 Subprocessors and supply chain E02 does not identify subservice organizations or inclusive/carve-out treatment. Obtain current subprocessor/hosting list, service/data/access roles, locations, downstream assurance and control flow-down, change notice and review rights. Map dependencies to payroll data and recovery. Vendor relationship owner + architecture/security; before decision TPRM-IAM-01 Workforce and privileged access E04 is only a policy summary; no workforce access samples or review/revocation evidence. E03 concerns customer-admin MFA only and is not supplier workforce evidence. Request access/MFA standards, role model, privileged-account population and exception controls, approval/review samples, termination revocation evidence. Independently verify customer-side E03 condition. Vendor IAM owner + customer IAM owner; before privileged use TPRM-CHG-01 Change and configuration No configuration standard, approval/deployment sample, emergency-change record or customer notification evidence supplied. Request scoped change procedure and redacted normal/emergency change samples with approval, testing, deployment and customer-impact notice. Vendor service/engineering owner; before decision or time-bound condition TPRM-OPS-01 Logging and monitoring No log source, retention, tamper protection, review sample, alert or customer-access/notification process. Obtain scoped event/logging coverage, access protection, retention, monitoring escalation, investigation evidence path and contractual availability. Vendor security operations owner; before decision or condition with controls TPRM-IR-01 Incident coordination No incident response plan, notification terms, contacts, exercise or evidence-preservation detail. Request plan/exercise summary, 24x7 contacts, contractual notification clock, customer coordination, evidence preservation and lessons learned. Confirm response obligations with legal. Vendor incident lead + customer incident coordinator; before production TPRM-RES-01 Continuity and recovery No service-specific BCP/DR, backup scope, restore test, recovery objectives or dependency record supplied. Payroll operational importance is a case assumption. Obtain service BCP/DR and redacted restore exercise, backup protection/retention, tested RTO/RPO, dependencies, customer responsibilities and outage communications. Validate business tolerances. Vendor continuity owner + payroll service owner; before decision TPRM-REV-01 Findings and reassessment recommendation_draft.md records three proposed findings and owners/dates; the decision and external feedback remain pending. E02-v2/E03-v2 are lab-only changes. Record authorized disposition, evidence versions, risk rationale, accepted exceptions, action tracking, reassessment triggers and reviewer sign-off. Do not mark real closure from mock retests. Risk owner + authorized reviewer; before production Risk rationale and treatment register Scenario: privileged credential compromise or malicious/erroneous change exposes payroll identities and bank details, or disrupts payroll processing. This is a plausible threat scenario based on data sensitivity and service dependency, not an observed threat or incident. Inherent likelihood: Medium (proposed qualitative rating) because a cloud payroll service has remote access and administrative dependencies, but the packet contains no threat intelligence, attack-surface evidence or control testing to calibrate probability. Inherent impact: High (proposed) due to sensitive financial/personnel data and payroll availability consequences; business impact and legal obligations require owner validation. These ratings are prioritization judgments, not calculated metrics. Residual risk: unassessed. Current assurance, operational controls, actual customer configuration, contract terms, downstream parties and recovery evidence are insufficient to judge control effectiveness. Do not infer residual risk from the synthetic control flags or platform status. Finding Current disposition Proposed treatment / closure evidence Owner / proposed date --- --- --- --- CERT-EXPIRY Open: E01 expired before review and unauthenticated Obtain current verifiable certificate/equivalent assurance; independently check issuer/accreditation, entity, payroll scope, validity/status and exclusions. Preserve review record. Vendor relationship owner / 23 Nov 2026 ASSURANCE-SCOPE Open: E02 v1 excludes payroll; E02-v2 is only a mock field edit Obtain genuine applicable report and review boundary, period, opinion, exceptions/responses, subservice method and CUECs. Assess bridge gap. Vendor relationship owner / 23 Nov 2026 CUSTOMER-MFA Initial mock gap; revised mock does not verify real enforcement Customer IAM owner to enable and verify MFA over all in-scope privileged accounts, document exceptions and retain dated evidence before any real use. Customer IAM owner / 20 Nov 2026 Contract/data protection Evidence not supplied; not scored as a control failure Review executed terms/DPA: purpose, data categories, roles, location/transfers, retention/deletion, breach notices, subprocessors, audit rights and return at exit. Procurement/legal + privacy / before contract Incident/continuity Evidence not supplied; unknown Obtain service-specific plans, exercises, contacts, RTO/RPO and dependency evidence; align contractual requirements with business tolerances. Vendor + customer service owners / before production Dates are proposed exercise targets, not agreed commitments. The original treatment catalog and generated memo remain the machine-readable workflow baseline; this narrative adds analytical context without claiming real remediation or human approval. Decision record and boundaries - Evidence considered: E01, E02 v1 and v2, E02-B scenario, E03 v1 and v2, E04, and the fictional case scope. - Approval / risk acceptance / named reviewer: Pending. No approval is implied by this draft. - Peer/mentor feedback and response: Pending; no feedback supplied. - Reassessment triggers: receipt of authenticated evidence; material change in service, data, hosting or subprocessors; incident; failed customer control; material contract change; or scheduled review. - This work product demonstrates structured document analysis, scoped evidence review, gap treatment and decision writing. It does not demonstrate a completed real-vendor review, client presentation, actual control testing at a supplier, or independent audit assurance.

title: Decision brief
text:
Synthetic portfolio exercise · 16 November 2026 · Draft, approval pending
All organizations, evidence, dates, roles and facts are fictional. This brief is not an actual vendor decision, audit, or supplier assurance opinion. Executive view Recommendation: hold production onboarding while decision-critical evidence is obtained and reviewed. The proposed payroll SaaS would process employee identities, payroll details and bank-account data. The lab assigns it High criticality because of that sensitivity and operational dependency; the business owner must validate the tier. The evidence packet does not establish current, authentic assurance for the payroll service. The first SOC-style summary explicitly excludes payroll; its revised version changes a synthetic scope field only. The ISO certificate metadata is expired and unauthenticated. Separately, the customer-owned privileged MFA requirement is disabled in the initial mock state; a revised mock is not real configuration evidence. This recommendation identifies evidence uncertainty, not proof of compromise or control failure. Onboarding could be reconsidered after current in-scope independent assurance—or a security-reviewer-validated alternative evidence package proportionate to the service—is reviewed, contractual/privacy and subprocessor diligence is complete, customer MFA is demonstrated, and continuity/incident obligations are reviewed. An ISO certificate alone would not answer operational-control, contract, subprocessor or continuity questions. Any conditional exception requires an accountable human risk owner's approval, compensating safeguards, time limits and escalation/stop criteria. Only an authorized business risk owner can approve onboarding or accept residual risk. Options Choice Benefit Main condition / trade-off Current fit --- --- --- --- Approve onboarding Supports service start Requires current in-scope independent assurance or a reviewer-validated alternative evidence package, material terms and controls, and explicit risk authority Not supported Conditional onboarding May permit bounded progress Needs approved restrictions, minimum controls, compensating safeguards, clear deadlines, monitoring and stop criteria; exception requires accountable human approval A future option after evidence review Hold Prevents production reliance while material unknowns are resolved May delay the service; owner should confirm business impact and alternatives Recommended now Technical view for security, procurement and service owners 1. Assurance boundary: E02 v1 is a fictional Type II-style summary for a support portal only and excludes payroll. A Type II period ending 30 September is not current assurance for later operation. The actual report, opinion, criteria, tests, exceptions and management responses are absent. E02-v2 is a workflow fixture, not a report revision. 2. Downstream services and customer conditions: no subservice organization list or inclusive/carve-out method is supplied. Obtain the actual report schedules and map material hosting dependencies. Review CUECs; the E03 MFA requirement is explicitly customer-operated in this case and must not be charged as a vendor failure. 3. Bridge gap: E02-B is only a hypothetical management statement. A real bridge letter could describe management's view of changes but would not extend the independent examination or test controls after the report period. Verify signatory authority and corroborate incidents and material changes. 4. ISO claim: E01's stated 31 October 2026 expiry predates the review. Its issuer, accreditation chain, certificate number and authoritative status are missing. Validate current record, entity, sites, exact ISMS scope and exclusions. Expiry is an assurance gap, not breach evidence. 5. Other diligence: E04 says a policy exists but includes no operating samples. Obtain workforce-access and change evidence, logging/incident handling, service-specific backup/restore tests, contract/security schedule and DPA, data locations, subprocessors, incident terms, deletion/return and exit plan. Proposed actions Priority Action Proposed accountable role Proposed timing --- --- --- --- Decision gate Obtain genuine, current, in-scope assurance; review opinion, test results, exceptions, carve-outs and CUECs; verify ISO claim Vendor relationship owner + security reviewer Before decision Customer prerequisite Verify MFA enforcement on the full privileged customer account population, including exceptions and emergency accounts Customer IAM owner Before privileged use Contract/data Review agreement, security schedule and DPA for incident notice, audit evidence, data use/location, subprocessor changes, retention/deletion and exit Procurement/legal + privacy Before contract/production Operational resilience Review service-specific incident/continuity plans, contacts, exercise evidence, restore tests, RTO/RPO and dependencies Vendor and customer service owners Before production Governance Confirm criticality, accountable acceptance authority, action owners, reassessment triggers and review date Payroll service owner + risk owner Before disposition The target dates in the detailed review are proposed exercise dates and have not been agreed by any supplier or stakeholder. Residual risk remains unassessed until the missing evidence is reviewed. Five-minute presentation outline 1. 0:00–0:45 — Service and decision: explain payroll dependency, sensitive data, proposed High tier and ask for a hold/decision-owner discussion. 2. 0:45–2:00 — Evidence quality: show E01 expiry/authentication gap and E02 scope mismatch; distinguish the v2 mock from authentic assurance. 3. 2:00–3:00 — Shared responsibility and unknowns: clarify customer MFA, bridge-letter limit, subservice carve-out and absent contract/DPA/continuity evidence. 4. 3:00–4:15 — Risk and options: explain the plausible compromise/disruption scenario, qualitative inherent rating and why residual risk cannot yet be rated; compare approve/conditional/hold. 5. 4:15–5:00 — Decisions requested: confirm business criticality, evidence owners, contract gate, customer MFA owner and authorized decision maker; record questions and follow-up actions. Feedback record External stakeholder feedback: pending. No client, peer, mentor, or hiring-team presentation has occurred as part of this artifact. Record real questions, requested evidence, changes made and unresolved disagreements in [ ../case-study/feedback_template.md ](../case-study/feedback_template.md) only after an actual review. AI review or this presentation outline is not stakeholder feedback.

title: GRC platform integration
text: What it adds The synthetic HarborPay supplier case now has a native Findings Assessment in CISO Assistant, with three native Finding records, their proposed remediation text, links to the applicable seeded Applied Controls , and links to synthetic Evidence inventory records. The existing supplier Entity Assessment remains in_review ; the product model has no direct EntityAssessment-to-FindingsAssessment relation, so the records are related by matching supplier context and provenance rather than claiming a native foreign-key association. Each of the ten scoped supplier controls stays to_do . Findings remain identified, severity is undefined, and the evidence objects are explicitly missing because no authentic vendor artifacts were supplied. The recommendation remains hold onboarding and human approval remains pending. These object types follow the product's native model instead of representing issues as completed controls or risk acceptances. This is a local, synthetic workflow demonstration. It does not establish enterprise GRC platform implementation experience, a production deployment, an actual supplier decision, or an audit opinion. Provenance and safety The sync consumes only output/assessment.json and output/control_review.json , mounted read-only into the backend. It hashes parsed JSON using canonical JSON serialization ( canonical-json-v1 ) so Windows and Linux line endings produce the same digest, then records those hashes in each managed finding's observation and the Findings Assessment description. Each attached Evidence item says it is a synthetic inventory placeholder and is created in missing state without an attachment. The deterministic VAD-SYN- references make repeated syncs idempotent. The integration fails closed if the case stops being fictional, its recommendation changes, the scoped records are absent, or an existing managed record's fields or relations no longer match the integration's expected state. It does not update existing findings in place, overwrite manual edits, mark a control effective, close a finding, approve evidence, or accept risk. If the source or a managed record changes, investigate and reconcile deliberately rather than rerunning blindly. Run against the local Docker stack From the repository root in PowerShell: powershell $repo = (Resolve-Path .).Path $linuxRepo = '/mnt/' + $repo.Substring(0, 1).ToLowerInvariant() + '/' + $repo.Substring(3).Replace('\', '/') $stage = "docker run --rm --volumes-from backend:rw -v '$linuxRepo/scripts:/scripts:ro' -v '$linuxRepo/output:/input:ro' alpine:3.23 sh -c 'mkdir -p /code/db/vad_data && cp /scripts/docker_sync_assessment.py /scripts/docker_verify_sync.py /scripts/docker_test_sync_safety.py /code/db/ && cp /input/assessment.json /input/control_review.json /code/db/vad_data/'" wsl.exe -d Ubuntu-24.04 -u root -- bash -lc $stage wsl.exe -d Ubuntu-24.04 -u root -- bash -lc 'docker exec backend python /code/db/docker_sync_assessment.py' wsl.exe -d Ubuntu-24.04 -u root -- bash -lc 'docker exec backend python /code/db/docker_verify_sync.py' wsl.exe -d Ubuntu-24.04 -u root -- bash -lc 'docker exec backend python /code/db/docker_test_sync_safety.py' wsl.exe -d Ubuntu-24.04 -u root -- bash -lc 'docker exec backend python /code/db/docker_verify_sync.py >/dev/null 2>&1' wsl.exe -d Ubuntu-24.04 -u root -- bash -lc "docker exec backend cat /tmp/platform_sync.json > '$linuxRepo/output/platform_sync.json'" Run the sync command again, then the verification command again. The second sync should report zero created and three unchanged findings. docker_test_sync_safety.py checks that a changed supplier identity is rejected, a same-count wrong evidence link fails exact-link verification, and a manual finding status edit is preserved while sync refuses to overwrite it; test mutations run inside rolled-back database transactions. The verifier emits a canonical record snapshot digest; it should be identical across readbacks when records have not changed. It exits nonzero on detected drift. The repo's ignored private Docker credentials are not read or printed by these commands. Native object mapping Training case item CISO Assistant object Treatment --- --- --- Vendor due-diligence review Existing EntityAssessment Preserved in review; no direct FK to findings register in upstream model Findings register FindingsAssessment Stable ref VAD-SYN-FINDINGS-HPD-2026-001 , in review; linked by case/supplier context Expired assurance metadata Finding Identified, undefined severity; maps to TPRM-REV-01 Assurance scope mismatch Finding Identified, undefined severity; maps to TPRM-REV-01 and TPRM-SUP-01 Customer-operated MFA condition Finding Identified, undefined severity; maps to TPRM-IAM-01 ; not attributed to vendor controls Synthetic baseline/retest evidence references Evidence missing , synthetic inventory only, no attachment; linked to finding Proposed next steps Finding recommendation Human action required; no automatic closure The TPRM- questions retain their proposed NIST CSF 2.0 and ISO/IEC 27001:2022 references as scoping aids. They are not native control mappings to verified framework catalog records, and no compliance equivalence is claimed. Verification limits The verifier checks counts, states, link targets, input hashes, and a stable digest of the read-back records. A repeat run tests idempotence and supports detection of manual drift; it is not a concurrency lock against another writer changing the database between separate command runs. All supplier data and evidence are fictional. A hiring résumé may describe this as a local CISO Assistant integration prototype with native findings, remediation, evidence-state and control relationships—not as client GRC implementation or verified vendor assurance.

title: Review walkthrough
text: Start with the business decision "I assessed whether a fictional payroll supplier could be onboarded. Because it handles employee identity and bank details, I reviewed whether its assurance evidence covered the purchased service and whether the customer had met its own responsibilities." Show the initial findings Open Evidence, select Initial review and inspect E01-E04. Explain: - The certificate date is expired. That means current assurance has not been established; it does not prove a security incident. - The report scope excludes payroll. A recent report for a different service cannot answer the question being assessed. - Customer administrator MFA is a customer-owned responsibility. Assigning every issue to the vendor would create the wrong remediation plan. - The policy passes only the documented presence/date/scope checks. It does not demonstrate that access reviews operated effectively. Show the retest and explain the limit Switch Findings to Retest. E02-v2 and E03-v2 address two selected checks. They become Ready for review. The expired-assurance finding stays Open. A passing automated check does not silently close a finding or approve onboarding. Make the recommendation Open Decision and download the memo. Explain the business impact of proceeding versus delaying payroll onboarding, what evidence remains missing, who owns the next action and who must decide. The recommendation is a hold pending an authorized review, not an actual supplier rejection. Ask for a real challenge Ask a peer/mentor: "Would you hold onboarding or allow a limited exception, and what evidence or business constraint would change your decision?" Record their actual answer in the feedback template. Revise one part of the recommendation or document why you retained it. Keep the earlier memo so the change is visible. Do not record a fictional stakeholder name or claim that automated code review was a client presentation. Explain the measurements Show Results: seeded gaps identified, no finding on the clean record, owner/date coverage and selected checks passing on revised evidence. Distinguish these lab measurements from business risk reduction. If asked about a GRC platform, use only the actual execution/configuration evidence available in platform/ .

title: Review methodology
text: Boundary and purpose This is an explicitly synthetic case used to practise third-party cyber-risk review. It is not a certification, assurance report review, legal opinion, or real vendor decision. The purpose is to evaluate evidence against a stated service, surface uncertainty, assign follow-up, and make a documented recommendation for human review. Evidence statuses - Present : a record exists; this does not mean it is genuine or adequate. - In scope : the record covers the named service and entity being assessed. - Current : dates satisfy the lab's stated assessment-date rule. - Verified : a reviewer performed and recorded an authenticity/integrity check. In this fixture, every vendor document remains unverified synthetic content. - Gap : a required fact is missing, expired, out of scope, or a stated responsibility is unmet. A gap is an evidence/control issue, not proof of a breach. - Retest eligible : updated evidence may address a specific finding. A reviewer checks its linkage, scope and adequacy before changing the status. Do not collapse missing, not verified, expired and out of scope into a “pass.” Record the exact evidence ID and version with every assessment result. The implemented fixture compares a baseline and one revision per evidence item. Additional rounds must use a new case; deeper revision chains are rejected so an intermediate failure cannot silently disappear. The selected metadata checks also require the certificate entity and customer MFA control/owner to match the assessment. The lab defines a maximum age of 365 days for policy approval and the end of the assurance-report period, configurable in data.json . These are training review thresholds, not ISO or SOC requirements. Passing these selected checks does not establish a document's authenticity or sufficiency for a complete assessment. Criticality and risk scenario The case proposes High criticality because the payroll service processes employee identity and bank account details and supports an important business function. A reviewer must confirm that tier for the fictional organization and explain any adjustment. Record a scenario in plain language, for example: “If privileged payroll access is misused or compromised, employee data could be exposed and payroll service disrupted.” Evaluate likelihood and impact separately using the organization's selected matrix. The numbers below are anchors for discussion, not default ratings for the three seeded gaps. Likelihood anchors Score Meaning ---: --- 1 Rare: requires unusual conditions; little relevant evidence 2 Unlikely: possible, with limited supporting evidence 3 Possible: plausible given the described exposure or weakness 4 Likely: strong indicators or repeated conditions support the scenario 5 Almost certain: direct, current evidence indicates the event is occurring or imminent Impact anchors Score Meaning ---: --- 1 Negligible: little service or data impact 2 Minor: limited, recoverable operational or confidentiality effect 3 Moderate: material team/customer effect requiring coordinated response 4 Major: broad sensitive-data or sustained service impact 5 Severe: critical business disruption or extensive sensitive-data impact Use the actual GRC instance's configured matrix for its own calculation. If it differs, record its name/version and scoring method rather than translating scores without justification. Do not invent a percentage reduction, set residual risk automatically, or rate an expired certificate itself as a breach. The expired record means current assurance has not been established. Treatment and approval For each finding, record evidence, effect on the assessed service, severity rationale, treatment, named role owner, due date, and retest evidence needed. Assign customer-operated CUECs to the customer owner; supplier duties and customer duties must not be conflated. Only a reviewer with decision authority should accept risk, approve an exception, close a finding, or authorize onboarding. Preserve the original assessment and the review history. A closure requires evidence matched to the finding plus a written review reason. The synthetic E02-v2 and E03-v2 can qualify only for simulated re-review of their respective checks; CERT-EXPIRY remains open. Lab evaluation Before reviewing the application output, compare it with expected_checks.json . Measure seeded-gap recall, clean-fixture findings, owner/due-date and evidence-link coverage, simulated retest closure, and whether the unresolved assurance gap stays open. Record actual numerator and denominator and inspect every mismatch. These are fixture-level process measures; they do not establish real-world accuracy or business risk reduction.

title: Assessment questionnaire
text:
SYNTHETIC TRAINING DATA. HarborPay Demo, its payroll service, evidence, roles, dates, and control states are fictional. This questionnaire is a study aid, not a supplier attestation, audit opinion, certification, or legal determination. Assessment date: 16 November 2026
In-scope service: Payroll processing SaaS
Data: Employee identity, payroll, and bank account details
Proposed criticality: High, subject to reviewer confirmation For every response, cite an evidence ID/version, state what it demonstrates, identify uncertainty, and assign an owner or follow-up where needed. “Not provided” and “not verified” do not mean “passed.” Review question Case evidence Initial reviewer prompt --- --- --- --- 1 Is the service and its data use clear enough to determine the review scope and business impact? Vendor/service description in data.json Confirm payroll is the service assessed and employee/bank data are in scope. Identify the business owner. 2 Is the security policy evidence present, owned, approved, and relevant to payroll? E04 Verify the named owner, approval date, review frequency, and service scope. Do not infer that the policy was followed in practice. 3 Is current ISO assurance evidence available, authentic, and in scope? E01 Check stated entity, service, expiry, and verification limitations. Request current authenticated evidence; do not equate an expired date with a control failure. 4 Does the assurance summary cover payroll and the relevant service boundary? E02; simulated retest E02-v2 Compare included/excluded services with the contracted payroll scope. Distinguish the synthetic scope test from an actual auditor-issued SOC report. 5 Which customer-operated controls are required, and are they met? E03; simulated retest E03-v2 Identify the customer owner, covered privileged accounts, initial mock state, and evidence needed for a real verification. 6 What decision, treatment, owner, due date, and reassessment trigger are justified? Findings and reviewer notes Explain likelihood/impact with evidence. State remaining uncertainty and obtain human approval for acceptance or onboarding. Reassessment notes Keep v1 evidence intact. Review E02-v2 and E03-v2 against their original gap, recording the reviewer, date, rationale, and resulting status. Leave CERT-EXPIRY open until current evidence is supplied and independently checked. title: E01 — ISO/IEC 27001 certificate claim (synthetic summary)
text:
Fictional supplier: HarborPay Demo
Claimed standard/version: ISO/IEC 27001:2022
Claimed certification period: 1 November 2025–31 October 2026
Claimed scope: “Information security management system supporting HarborPay Demo payroll processing SaaS.”
Issuer, accreditation body, certificate number, signature and verification URL: Not supplied. This is a constructed summary of a certificate claim, not a certificate image and not an independently authenticated record. The entity name and scope wording are hypothetical. No certification body or accreditation status is asserted. Reviewer analysis The stated expiry precedes the assessment date (16 November 2026), so E01 cannot establish current certification on the review date. Even within its stated dates, reliance would require checking the certificate against the issuing body's authoritative directory, confirming the legal entity and relevant locations, reading the exact scope and exclusions, and checking the issuer/accreditation chain and certificate status. A standard name alone does not establish that payroll processing, the relevant hosting boundary, or every subcontractor was covered. Treat CERT-EXPIRY as an assurance freshness and authenticity gap . Expiry or missing verification is not evidence that a security control failed, that a breach occurred, or that the supplier is unsafe. Request current independently verifiable evidence and preserve this original record; do not silently replace its dates.

title: E02-B — management bridge-letter scenario (synthetic)
text: Fictional authoring role: HarborPay Demo management. No real supplier communication exists. For this exercise, assume management states that no material changes to the payroll service control environment came to its attention between 1 October and 16 November 2026, while directing customers to the prior-period assurance report. No signed letter, responsible executive, incident log, change inventory, or corroborating records are supplied; this is a scenario prompt, not evidence that management actually made the statement. Review treatment A bridge letter is management representation for a gap after a report period. It does not extend the independent examination period, test controls during the gap, establish that exceptions were remediated, or substitute for a current report. Evaluate the named signatory's authority, exact dates and service boundary, meaning of “material change,” security incidents, significant control changes and subprocessor changes; corroborate with appropriate records where available. Record the interval after 30 September as an assurance limitation until verified. Do not treat this hypothetical statement as evidence of no incidents or no change.

title: E02 — SOC 2 Type II-style summary (synthetic exercise exhibit)
text: > This is original fictional training text, not an AICPA SOC 2 report, examination, auditor's opinion, or representation of a real service organization's controls. No auditor or CPA is named or simulated. Exhibit facts - Purported period: 1 January–30 September 2026. - Purported report type: Type II-style description for the exercise. The actual report, opinion, criteria, tests, samples, results, and exceptions schedule are not supplied. - E02 v1 boundary: Customer support portal. It explicitly excludes payroll processing. - E02-v2 lab revision: The synthetic scope field now lists customer support portal and payroll processing, and no excluded services. This is a field-level workflow retest only; it does not create an actual report or cure the missing report contents. - Opinion: Not provided. - Exceptions: Not represented in this short exhibit; unknown, not “none.” - Subservice organizations: Method (inclusive or carve-out), names, services and complementary subservice-organization controls are not provided. - CUECs: No actual report schedule is supplied. The separately modelled E03 customer MFA requirement is a proposed case control, not a claim that a real SOC report listed it. How to reason about it Type II assurance ordinarily concerns whether described controls were suitably designed and operated over a specified period, as assessed in an actual report. A summary label and date range do not establish that such an examination occurred. The date range is historical and ends 30 September 2026; it does not on its own establish conditions after that date. First obtain the genuine report under appropriate confidentiality controls, then examine the service/system description, criteria, auditor's opinion, test procedures and results, exceptions and management responses, subservice-organization treatment, and CUECs. For v1, scope mismatch is decisive: a support-portal summary cannot support a conclusion about the payroll service merely because both are associated with the same hypothetical supplier. For v2, a changed declaration makes the fixture eligible for a simulated scope-field check only. It leaves authenticity, actual scope language, period coverage, exceptions, report opinion and control testing unresolved. Do not describe either version as passing a real SOC review.
